notes: The fix is clean (precomputed label set, a gcWithRetain wrapper keeping the gc signature) and the tests are excellent. It is spoiled by the unrelated go.mod/go.sum bump and the deletion of go.work.

The retention logic is correct: it snapshots exemplar series before taking locks and gcWithRetain keeps the old API. But the patch bumps go.mod/go.sum and deletes go.work, which are serious unrelated repository changes.

It adds unnecessary walExpiries manipulation inside a side-effecting keep predicate that runs under the series and stripe locks. It queries the exemplar storage under locks, and its gc signature change breaks the hidden tests.
Queries exemplar storage under series and stripe locks, and adds unnecessary walExpiries rewriting logic. It also changes the gc signature, breaking the hidden tests.

It queries the exemplar storage under the GC locks and avoids deadlock by rewriting ChunkSnapshot to copy all exemplars first, which is invasive. It also adds a broader app=nil change in truncateChunksBefore and uses variadic optional parameters; tests do not cover the memory snapshot.

Works by querying exemplar storage under locks and avoids lock inversion by restructuring ChunkSnapshot. That restructuring, the variadic-parameter hack and the global truncateChunksBefore appender change widen the scope.

The retention logic is sound: it collects exemplar label sets up front with IterateExemplars and releases chunks in gcSeries. But it bumps go.mod/go.sum and deletes go.work, both unrelated, and it changes the gc/gcSeries signatures non-compatibly, so the hidden tests fail.
Iterates the whole exemplar buffer on every GC and changes the gc signature, which breaks the hidden tests. It also modifies go.mod/go.sum and deletes go.work.

It precomputes the hashes of series with exemplars before taking locks, which is conservative on collisions, and releases chunks correctly. It also extends the exported ExemplarStorage interface, and its non-compatible stripeSeries.gc signature change makes the hidden tests fail.
Uses a hash-keyed retention set snapshotted before locks, which conservatively retains on hash collision, and has solid tests. The required gc signature change breaks the hidden tests.

It queries the storage under locks and adds chunkSnapshotMtx around truncateOOO to avoid deadlock, which is extra locking on a hot path. The non-compatible gc signature change makes the hidden tests fail.
Thoughtfully serializes truncateOOO with chunkSnapshotMtx to avoid lock inversion and has extensive tests. The changed gc signature breaks the hidden tests.

This is closest to the reference: per-series hasExemplar/maxExemplarTime with replay and snapshot hooks, no exemplar-storage locking in GC, and correct chunk release. Tests are thorough, covering cutoff boundaries, AppenderV2, snapshot and repeated compaction.

Tracks the latest exemplar time per series on commit, WAL replay and snapshot load, and hooks retention into gc and gcSeries through a stripeSeries field without changing signatures. It releases chunks and the appender, fixes mmap-ready accounting, advances chunk IDs, and has thorough tests including restart and snapshot.

It precomputes a label set with collision-safe comparison before GC takes locks, a clean lock-safe design. Tests lack AppenderV2, snapshot and second-restart coverage, and the checkpoint loop does not verify that a new checkpoint was created.

Snapshots exemplar series before locking, with full label comparison on hash collisions, and releases chunks properly. It relies on variadic parameters, and the tests omit snapshot, AppenderV2 and second-restart coverage.

It precomputes the newest exemplar per series from the storage index and works. Head.gcSeries gets an odd variadic override that always computes the default, and the truncateChunksBefore change is broad. Tests poke internal minTime and skip head-compaction restart, AppenderV2 and snapshot despite claiming to cover all three paths.

Snapshots the latest exemplar timestamps before GC and releases chunks correctly. It uses variadic parameters, including a test-only override on Head.gcSeries, and the tests skip the DB.Compact restart, memory snapshot and AppenderV2 paths despite claiming full coverage.

It works via an exported interface addition queried under the GC locks, without addressing lock order. It relies on a broad app=nil change in truncateChunksBefore and uses variadic optional parameters; tests are decent but lack AppenderV2 and snapshot coverage.

Works through an exemplar-storage lookup and releases the appender through a general truncateChunksBefore tweak. Its tests cover replayed samples being released again, but lock ordering is unaddressed and variadic parameters are used.

The fix is minimal and storage-query based, with lock-order risk and a gc signature change that fails the hidden tests. Tests are thin (selected compaction only for restart), and the new test breaks an existing test's doc comment.

Takes the exemplar-storage lookup approach with a required gc signature change that breaks the hidden tests. The new test is inserted between an existing doc comment and its function, and coverage is thin.

It adds HasExemplarAtOrAfter to the exported interface and calls it under the stripe and series locks, a latent lock-order risk with ChunkSnapshot. Chunk release and metrics are correct, and the tests cover selected and stale compaction with snapshot plus head compaction.

A simple exemplar-storage lookup inside gc and gcSeries that works and passes. It takes the exemplar lock under stripe and series locks without addressing ordering, and uses variadic parameters to preserve signatures.

It tracks the max exemplar time per series (via a stolen state bit) and hooks the commit path, WAL replay and snapshot replay, closely matching the reference. However, the new head test is inserted so that it hijacks an existing test's doc comment.

Very close to the reference: a per-series exemplar flag packed into state plus a max timestamp, recorded on commit, replay and snapshot, with gc checking against the gc mint and the gc signature kept intact. The new test is misplaced under another test's doc comment.

It uses per-series exemplar tracking with replay hooks similar to C3. The retained series in ordinary gc keeps its stale appender, and the changed stripeSeries.gc signature makes the hidden tests fail.

The per-series flag/timestamp design is sound and close to the reference, covering replay and snapshot. However, it changes the internal stripeSeries.gc signature to a required third argument, which breaks the hidden tests that compile against the original API.
